pages.text: "What does Grandma look like again?" Bami pressed their beak to the window at Grandma's station. They hadn't met in a long time. White-flowering trees bloomed on the platform.
Grandma Owl boarded with a big bundle. "My Bami!" Bami shyly hid behind Mom's apron. "Hello..." A tiny voice. "I want to stay by you, Mom," they whispered.
The train would wait a while to take on water. Grandma sat by the window; Bami peeked from behind the door. Her voice and smell felt unfamiliar. "When will she get off?" Bami felt glum.
Grandma opened the bundle. Out came steaming sweet potatoes. "I steamed these this morning for you." One bite filled Bami's beak with sweetness.
Next came a new teal scarf. "I knitted the one around your neck, too. It's getting small, so I made another." Bami looked down. "You made this?"
Mom whispered, "Grandma spent days getting ready for your visit." At the bundle's bottom was a picture of baby Bami in Grandma's arms. She had thought about Bami so much. Their heart stirred.
Bami hurried into Grandma's arms. "Grandma!" Her hug was the softest and warmest in the world. Bami opened their wings. Grandma sang, "Grandma's station, a snuggly hug!"
That evening, all three sat in the dining car as Grandma rode along. Grandma's old stories, Mom's pancakes—Bami stayed close, laughing. Grandma wasn't unfamiliar anymore.

Next morning, the train returned to Grandma's station. She had to leave. Bami, shy yesterday, now felt tears at parting. "Come again!" They hugged on the platform. "One, Grandma's station! Two, a snuggly hug! Three, see you again!"

As the train left, Mom cuddled Bami. "You love Grandma now!" Sharing their hearts had brought them close. Grandma's station, a snuggly hug! With the new scarf wrapped once around, Bami watched Grandma through the window.
